title: draft-atwood-mimi-calls: a cascade from the parent is not an immediate loss of media
description:
Found while deciding mimid-1wgh.111, and it is a correction to the
draft rather than a mimid note.

§4.4 of draft-atwood-mimi-calls says "A participant removed from the
call loses access to subsequent media at once, because the epoch they
were removed in is the last one whose secret they can compute. No
media-layer rekeying protocol is needed to achieve it."

That is true of a removal FROM THE CALL, which is a Commit in the call's
own group and so changes the epoch. It is NOT true of the cascade
room-policy §5 describes, where a user leaving the PARENT should leave
the parent-dependent children too: a hub is not an MLS member and cannot
commit, so the best it can do is propose the removal and wait for a
member's next Commit (decision mimid-1wgh.111). Until that Commit, the
departed user is still in the call's group and can still derive the
media secret.

So the draft currently promises something it does not deliver for one of
the two ways a participant leaves, and a reader would reasonably assume
otherwise, since §4.1 ties the call room to the parent.

PROPOSED: in §4.4, distinguish the two. A removal from the call takes
effect in the Commit that makes it. A removal that follows from leaving
the parent takes effect when a member of the call next commits, because
the hub that notices the parent change is not a member of the child
group. Say the window exists rather than leaving it to be discovered,
and note it in Security Considerations beside the entitlement argument,
which is where a reader looks for exactly this kind of gap.

Writing it is a jmap-chat-spec-adjacent edit to Mark's own I-D repo and
needs his OK, like any other.
